correctness.rationale: The carry identity holds for every j and gives a mandatory +1 in any two consecutive transitions. Oppositely ordered triples then force zero net increment. A reversible long factor must be two-periodic; when it is a nonpalindromic even-length factor, one reversed orientation necessarily forces two -1 increments within three successive positions, excluded by divisibility by b>=3 or by 4 when b=2,m>=3. Exact residue/congruence witnesses prove the full length-two factor language and its orbit counts. The verifier successfully executed 3477 independent finite assertions; the proof, not finite tests, establishes the infinite conclusion.
